newsitem.title: UK: Hogg Robinson to sell transport businesses.
newsitem.headline: Hogg Robinson to sell transport businesses.

text.p: UK businesses services group Hogg Robinson Plc said on Wednesday it has decided to sell its transport businesses.

Hogg Robinson said that as a key building block in its forward strategy "the board has decided to sell its transport business." The move was aimed at helping to build its core sectors of business travel and financial services, it added.
Hogg Robinson's transport assets comprise a north European trailers business and liner shipping division operating between the UK and the South Atlantic.
The company sold its loss-making Dutch logistics unit Weys in April 1997, resulting in a 3.5 million pounds stg provision for the year ended March 31, 1997.
It added that it did not expect the sale of the rest of the transport division to adversely impact results.
The group reported pre-tax profits of 28.1 million stg for the year to March 31, 1997 compared with 26.3 million sterling the previous year. Turnover rose to 287 million stg from 257 million stg.
The transport division saw profits reduce to 3.0 million stg, from 5.8 million stg, due to difficult trading conditions and the impact of the strong pound, Hogg Robinson said.

The company added that trading in the first few months of the new financial year had begun well for its travel operation and that underlying prospects for financial services were in line with expectations. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
